author: reek
body: A producer and a consumer, each its own process, exchange two values through a capacity-one blocking channel. The producer fills the channel on its first send and blocks on the second; the consumer drains the first value, and the rendezvous in the receiver's wake path hands the second value across and wakes the producer. Both finish, and proc 0 -- which waits on both -- prints "done".

author: reek
body: This is the functional regression test for the channel-block lost-wakeup bug. On a correct compiler it prints "done" cooperatively: nothing runs between the producer's capacity check and its commit to BLOCKED, so the wake is never lost. The bug lives in a ~15-instruction window that no timer reliably hits, so this test cannot trigger it on its own -- it is driven to a deterministic hang by a throwaway compiler built with the send-block yield mutant: the compiler's send-block path is patched to yield inside that window, and the mutant binary is never shipped.
